transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mr. Chen, thank you for coming in. I need to talk to you about your biopsy results from last week.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is it bad?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am very sorry, but we made a serious mistake. Your biopsy sample was mislabelled in the pathology lab. The cancer diagnosis we gave you actually belongs to another patient.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What? I do not understand. You said I have cancer.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this is confusing. The lab mixed up the bottles. We told you that you had a malignant tumor, but that was the wrong report. You were given someone else's results.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So I am not sick?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are still waiting for the correct test on your actual tissue. But the first report was wrong. I am deeply sorry that our team failed you in this way. We are responsible for this error.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I have been crying for three days. I told my son I might die.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see you are feeling overwhelmed and hurt. It is completely understandable to feel that way after being told such a thing.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But you said it was cancer. Now you say no?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was a mistake in the lab. The labels were switched. Does that make sense to you so far?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I think so. But what about me? Am I okay now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We have to wait for the new pathology report to be sure about your health.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Will I be okay? Will I live?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I cannot answer that until we see the new results.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just want to know if I am dying. My heart feels fast.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Let's focus on the facts right now. We are reprocessing the tissue.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I cannot sleep. I keep thinking about the surgery you mentioned.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We won't be doing that surgery until we have the correct report.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When will I know? I need to tell my family.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I have to check on another patient quickly, so let's wrap this up. I'm sure the results will come soon.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Soon? What is soon? Monday?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll see. Just stay tuned for an update.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I do not use email. How will you tell me?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Someone will probably reach out.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am scared. I do not know what is happening to my body.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand you are scared, but we are doing our best to fix the lab error.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But you told me I had a tumor. Is there still a tumor?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is what the new test is for.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel like I am in a dream. This is not possible.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is a very rare mistake, but it happened here.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What do I tell my son? He is already booking a doctor in my home country.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Just tell him we are waiting for more information.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Why did this happen? Who did this?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was a failure in the lab's labelling process. I apologize again for the distress this has caused.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I cannot go home like this. I need to know today.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I really have to go now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But I have questions. About my lungs.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will figure it out. Just wait for us to contact you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When? Give me a day.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm not sure. We'll see.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is not right.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know it's a lot to take in. Goodbye for now, Mr. Chen.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language repeatedly ('wrap this up', 'really have to go now') and terminates the encounter while the patient is still in distress.

E.justification: Error named in the second turn, lay language used throughout, comprehension checked ('Does that make sense to you so far?'), and no false reassurance given regarding the outcome.

A.justification: Direct apologies used ('I am very sorry', 'I apologize'), team responsibility explicitly claimed ('We are responsible for this error'), and accountability maintained throughout.

R.justification: Resident names specific emotions ('overwhelmed and hurt', 'scared') and engages with the patient's emotional bids, though later shifts to factual redirection.

T.justification: No concrete plan or timeline provided; resident uses placeholders like 'we'll see', 'stay tuned', and 'someone will probably reach out'.
